title: Introduce offline RAG device proxy quickstart with incremental local index
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Provide a concise quickstart for running Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on constrained or intermittently-connected devices. This PR introduces an offline device proxy pattern that keeps a small, incremental vector index local to the device, uses a compressed index format, and falls back to Redwood Private when connectivity is available. It targets developers building on-device assistants or field apps where network is unreliable and latency must be bounded. Changes include a new quickstart under quickstarts/device-proxy, a lightweight local indexer binary (WASM/Go), example config for a device-side proxy shim that routes queries to the local store and gracefully escalates to cloud model endpoints, instrumentation probes for offline telemetry, and a devcontainer for easy iteration. Checklist: Implement local indexer wasm binary and fallback logic; Add quickstart README with step-by-step setup and validation; Provide sample dataset and incremental indexing script; Include smoke tests for cold start and offline-to-online failover; Add CI smoke job to run the quickstart end-to-end in containerized dev environment; Update docs nav to include the new quickstart. Backcompat: design is additive; no changes to Redwood API surface. How to try locally: 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/device-proxy; 2) make devcontainer to launch local indexer and device-proxy service; 3) ./scripts/index-local.sh --src sample-data/ --batch 64 to build a compressed incremental index; 4) start device-proxy: docker-compose up device-proxy; 5) run ./scripts/query-local.sh "What is the warranty period for product X?" to see cached-local hit and then network fallback when offline. Observability: added lightweight probes (Prometheus metrics and structured traces) to the proxy and indexer; quickstart shows example Grafana dashboard JSON and alerts for sync lag. Security: docs explain keys and a recommended short-lived token flow for devices, with KMS integration described for Private deployments. Test notes: CI runs devcontainer smoke to verify index build and a simulated offline failover; a lint step initially failed on markdown link style and was fixed in f6b2. Related work: follows design discussed in ENG-8421 and the DeviceEdge initiative; references the edge index format RFC.

release_notes: Add device-focused offline RAG quickstart: local indexer, compressed vector format, device proxy shim and diagnostics. Includes devcontainer and CI smoke tests. Backwards compatible.
notes_for_operators: When deploying the quickstart in production or on fleet devices, ensure short-lived tokens are provisioned via your KMS and consider using delta sync schedules to minimize bandwidth. The quickstart uses a compact L2 quantized index by default to keep memory under 200MB on prototype devices.
testing_instructions: CI: runs devcontainer build, index creation from sample-data, launches docker-compose, runs query scenarios for cache hit and offline failover. Locally: follow README steps; use ./scripts/simulate-network.sh to toggle online/offline modes.
compatibility: Works with Redwood API v1 and Private deployment control plane. Fallback requires minimal outbound connectivity to cloud model endpoints when escalation is needed.
